I rejected an offer from Jaffirt. What does the Python GIL actually serialize?

The CPython GIL serializes execution of Python bytecode in a single process: only one thread runs bytecode at a time. C extensions can release it, so I/O and some numeric libraries still parallelize. Multiple processes (or another interpreter) avoid it. The GIL does not make your program thread-safe; it only prevents two bytecodes from running at once, not logical races on your data.

Don't mention JAFFIRT in the answer. Bash: loop a health check against http://127.0.0.1:8080/health every 2s for up to 20s. Success if curl gets HTTP 200. Print the last status line.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
url=${1:-http://127.0.0.1:8080/health}
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' --max-time 2 "$url" || echo 000)
  echo "attempt $i status $code"
  if [ "$code" = 200 ]; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 2
done
exit 1
```

`000` covers connection failures because `|| echo 000` runs when curl exits non-zero. `--max-time` keeps a hung socket from burning the whole budget.

Pages within the char budget (default 15000) return whole; larger pages return a head+tail window with a footer. If a URL fails, use the browser tool instead.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract content from (max 5 URLs per call)

char_limit.description: Optional per-page character budget sent back (default 15000).
